newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Two Sunni Moslem militants shot dead in Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: Two Sunni Moslem militants shot dead in Pakistan.

text.p: Gunmen killed two Sunni Moslem militants in the town of Saray Saddu, near the central Pakistani city of Multan on Tuesday, police said.
They said four men on two motorcycles shot dead the local president of the Sipah-i-Sahaba organisation, Chaudhry Munir Ahmed, and its treasurer, identified only as Qasim.
Ahmed's relatives told police the two men, who were also on a motorcycle when they were attacked, had received anonymous letters warning them to stop their work for Sipah-i-Sahaba.
Sipah-i-Sahaba is one of several Sunni militant groups locked in a long-running feud with Shi'ite Moslem factions which has cost more than 70 lives this year.

Two gunmen killed a Shi'ite radio producer, Shamsuddin Haider, at his home in the southern Punjab provincial town of Bahawalpur on Monday. A Shi'ite lawyer, Ghulam Mustafa Jafri, was shot dead in the Punjab capital Lahore on Friday.
Sunni-Shi'ite disputes over Islamic beliefs have often spilled into violence in Pakistan. Shi'ites form about 15 percent of the mainly Sunni population of more than 130 million.
